Health centre demolished at midnight in Dhaka
item.description:
The Radda MCH-FP Centre in Mirpur 1, Dhaka, was vandalised and looted at midnight after tying up security guards. More than 200 masked men entered the centre carrying locally made weapons and first held two security guards hostage. They then looted valuable equipment, medicines, vaccines, cash and other belongings. Later, the entire facility, including one concrete and three semi-concrete buildings, was demolished using heavy machinery.

The vandalism took place around midnight on Thursday. The attack was carried out under the banner of an organisation called “Sammona Dokandar Samabaya Samiti Limited”. Physician Nasrin Akhter, executive director of the Radda MCH-FP Centre, claimed that the damage amounted to more than Tk 10 million. She filed a case with Shah Ali police station as the plaintiff in connection with the incident.

Two factions of the local BNP had allegedly been trying to take control of the land for a long time. On Thursday night, one faction took control of it under the name Sammona Dokandar Samabaya Samiti Limited. Several local sources said BNP leader Ferdousi Ahmed Mishti, a lawmaker from a reserved women’s seat, is leading the faction. She is joint convener of Dhaka North City BNP. She is the wife of a deceased councillor and sister of a deceased BNP MP.

Officials of the vaccination centre alleged that they informed police during the attack and vandalism. Although police went to the scene, they failed to protect the facility. The entire building was demolished. However, Shah Ali police said legal action would be taken after investigation once a case was filed.

A visit to the site yesterday, Friday afternoon, found that the Radda MCH-FP vaccination centre was located between Muktijoddha Market and Fair Plaza Market, adjacent to Mirpur 1. The centre’s main gate was locked. Some construction materials, including bamboo and poles, were lying around. There was a signboard above the gate. It read, “Sammona Dokandar Samabaya Samiti Limited is the owner of this plot, allotted by the National Housing Authority of the Government of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh and registered in its name. The area of the land is 10 kathas.”

Later, going to the rear of the vaccination centre through a nearby alley, it was seen that the boundary wall of the centre had been demolished. Three concrete and semi-concrete buildings standing next to one another had also been demolished. Broken plaster, bamboo, poles and other construction materials were scattered around. The doors and windows of the rooms had been removed. Although some rooms still had doors, they bore marks of blows from sharp weapons. Furniture, medicines, vaccines and capsules from inside the rooms were scattered on the floor. There was a large mango tree in one corner of the premises. However, several of its branches had been cut off and left there. Curious crowd had gathered to look at the scene.

A shopkeeper next to the vaccination centre, speaking to Prothom Alo on condition of anonymity, said he closed his shop at 10pm and went home. When he returned in the morning, he found that nothing was left. Poor people could get vaccinated here at a low cost. But now it looks like a pile of rubble. Whoever did it, it was not a good thing.

Providing services for 50 years

The Radda MCH-FP Centre began its operations in 1974 to provide maternal and child healthcare services to disadvantaged and low-income people in Mirpur. The centre was launched at the initiative of Radda Barnen, an organisation of the then Swedish Save the Children. Currently, the organisation provides reproductive health and family planning services, antenatal and postnatal care, child vaccination, child healthcare and community health programmes. Its three permanent clinics also offer various testing facilities, including pathology, biochemistry and haematology, according to patients’ needs. Although its main centre is in the Mirpur 10 area, the organisation’s services extend to Mirpur 1, Bauniabad, Uttara, Bhasantek slum and Old Dhaka.

A local shopkeeper said on condition of anonymityHe closed his shop at 10pm and went home. When he returned in the morning, he found that nothing was left. Poor people could get vaccinated here at a low cost. But now it looks like a pile of rubble. Whoever did it, it was not a good thing.

Prominent industrialist and International Chamber of Commerce Bangladesh President Mahbubur Rahman is the chairperson of the organisation’s board of trustees, while social worker Tahurunnesa Abdullah, the first Bangladeshi woman to receive the Ramon Magsaysay Award, known as Asia’s Nobel, serves as treasurer. Former bureaucrat Abdul Mueed Chowdhury, prominent businessmen ASM Kasem and AKAzad, and former secretary Abdul Karim are also members of the board of trustees. Kazi Fazlur Rahman, adviser to the first caretaker government and a former secretary; renowned gynaecologist Professor TA Chowdhury; and engineer Professor Jamilur Reza Choudhury had served on the organisation’s board of trustees.

The organisation’s Executive Director Nasrin Akhter said some people had been trying to occupy the land in the name of Sammona Samabaya Samiti for the past five to six years. An attempt was also made in 2022, but they failed at the time. They came on Thursday night and demolished everything. The attack was carried out with the intention of occupying the land, she said.

Masked men attack

The first information report (FIR) filed over the vandalism and looting said that around midnight on Thursday, 200 to 250 masked men carrying sharpen weapons, hammers and sticks climbed over the wall and entered the premises. They beat two security guards at the vaccination centre, Andria Sarker and Abdul Hai. They later tied them to a pole. They took control of the entire building and prevented members of the public from entering. At one point, they broke the main gate and vandalised all the rooms of the building using heavy machinery used for demolishing buildings. The FIR names a man identified as Hanif Mia, 50.

The FIR also said the attackers took government EPI vaccines, government registers and documents related to vaccination, various family planning equipment and supplies, medicines and vaccines, two ultrasonography machines, a generator, two computers, a printer, three refrigerators, three air conditioners (ACs), three steel cupboards, CCTV cameras, chairs, tables and other furniture. The total damage amounted to Tk 10.9 million. Before leaving, the attackers put up a banner on the wall bearing the name “Sammona Dokandar Samabaya Samiti Limited”.

Two BNP factions had been trying to occupy the land

According to locals, shopkeepers and relevant sources, two factions of the local BNP had been trying to occupy the land for a long time. A case had also been filed over the land. As a result, no one had been able to occupy it for so long. Since the BNP came to power in 2026, attempts had again been made to occupy the land under the banner of Sammona Dokandar Samabaya Samiti. BNP leader Ferdousi Ahmed Mishti, a lawmaker from a reserved women’s seat, is leading the faction. Most recently, they demolished the institution and occupied the land on Thursday night.

Asked about this, Ferdousi Ahmed told Prothom Alo that she had also heard about the vandalism. She could not go there because she was busy. Although her name is associated with Sammona Dokandar Samabaya Samiti, she was not involved in the vandalism. Since a case has been filed over the vandalism, she said police should investigate the incident in accordance with the law.

Executive Director Nasrin Akhter told Prothom Alo that the Radda MCH-FP Centre had been providing free primary healthcare, maternity and family planning services to poor and helpless women and children for nearly 50 years in partnership with the government. She said it was an important healthcare centre for thousands of people in the area. They had been operating the institution under an agreement with the government. She said the government’s measles-rubella vaccination programme was scheduled to begin today. The institution was demolished just before that.

Shah Ali police station Officer-in-Charge Jahangir Alam told Prothom Alo that a case had been filed over the attack and vandalism. Appropriate legal action would be taken after investigating the incident.

item.title: PM reaffirms Bangladesh’s unwavering support for Palestinian right to self-determination
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has reaffirmed Bangladesh’s unwavering support for the legitimate demands of the Palestinian people, including their right to self-determination and to establish an independent State of Palestine.
“The people of Bangladesh, who cherish democracy, are deeply concerned about the suffering of the freedom-seeking Palestinian people,” he said on Thursday (New York time) while addressing the General Debate of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly at the UN HQ in New York.
“Bangladesh reaffirms its unwavering support for their legitimate demands, including their right to self-determination and their right to establish an independent State of Palestine,” said the prime minister.
He placed Bangladesh’s position on Palestine within his broader call for a peaceful and humane international order, stressing dialogue, diplomacy, mutual cooperation, equality, fairness and respect as the basis for relations among states in conflict.
“We aspire to a peaceful world, a humane global community where, rather than lethal weapons, reason and debate, diplomacy, education and humanity become the instruments of change,” he said.
Tarique Rahman said Bangladesh sees the United Nations as the centre of efforts to establish an understanding-based global community that respects the independence and sovereignty of one another.
He also reaffirmed Bangladesh’s support for UN initiatives aimed at establishing global humanity and world peace and reiterated the country’s commitment to general and complete disarmament, preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons and arms control.
The prime minister said human-made conflicts had created unrest in many parts of the world, leading to displacement and humanitarian crises, while wars and conflicts were putting severe pressure on the global economy.
“We believe that any conflict should be resolved through dialogue, diplomatic processes and mutual cooperation,” he said, adding that equality, fairness, protection of mutual interests, respect and dignity should form the basis of bilateral and multilateral relations among states in conflict.
Bangladesh’s position on Palestine came as the country also raised other humanitarian concerns at the UNGA, including the prolonged displacement of Rohingyas from Myanmar.
The prime minister said Bangladesh had been providing shelter to more than 1.2 million forcibly displaced Rohingyas for more than nine years and called for firm and effective international support for a lasting solution to the crisis.
He said the only solution was the safe return of the displaced Rohingya population to their homeland in Myanmar, while urging continued life-saving assistance until their repatriation.
On another global issue affecting Bangladesh and millions of people worldwide, Tarique Rahman called for stronger international cooperation to ensure the rights, dignity and welfare of migrants.
He said Bangladesh remained committed to regular, safe and orderly migration.
The prime minister also called for stronger global action on climate justice, climate finance and adaptation support, saying Bangladesh is among the countries most vulnerable to the adverse impacts of climate change despite making little contribution to global carbon emissions.

item.title: From the Amazon to Heyako: inside one of Asia’s largest rubber garden in Dantmara
item.description:
In late August of 2022, I embarked on a whirlwind visit to the greater Chittagong region. It was the only time I had ever made it to the picturesque Upazila of Fatikchhari. The weather was characteristically warm and highly humid with stray rains, aligning perfectly with the typical transition period from the peak monsoon into early autumn.
Featuring scenic tea and rubber gardens, rolling hills, and a rich spiritual heritage the fertile landscape of Fatikchhari sits as a wide valley between the Sitakunda Hills to the west and the Chittagong Hill Tracts to the east. Its topography transitions smoothly from elevated highlands to low-lying floodplains.
I had no clue whatsoever that traveling north from the port city—while visiting farmlands and talking to farmers about homegrown, eco-friendly agricultural practices—I would suddenly stumble upon a bustling rural market hub called Heyako. That chance encounter led me to Dantmara, one of Asia’s largest rubber gardens.
By midday, winding roads lined with dense rubber trees invited me deep into the sprawling, 4,500-acre estate, its thousands of trees fully flushed with heavy foliage. Entering the garden, I could clearly sense how early autumn was playing out in the vibrancy of the plantation.
In late August, the Dantmara Rubber Garden reaches its peak visual richness, completely transformed by the recently passed monsoon season. Autumn brings a sea of vibrant, deep green leaves. The sunlight filtering through the thick canopy is soft and dappled, creating a peaceful, muted green glow across the forest floor. The straight, slender trunks of the rubber trees stand in perfectly uniform, geometric rows. Thanks to the high humidity, the dark bark often looks slick and wet, lightly coated in bright green moss.
Planting rubber seeds in a germination bed is a critical first step in raising healthy rootstocks for budding, as rubber seeds have a very short viability period and must be sown immediately after collection. For germination bed typically a shady, flat, open area with close access to a water source, protected from strong winds and pests, is selected. Rubber seeds typically begin sprouting within 7 to 14 days. The sprouted seedlings are then immediately transplanted into a ground nursery or poly bags to grow into budded rootstocks. Photo: Dhaka Tribune/BFIDC
Over time, the area developed around the Heyako Bazar, which grew as a historic meeting place where indigenous hillside farmers brought local crops like ginger, turmeric, and pineapples to trade with plains merchants. As the marketplace thrived, the unique local name Heyako eventually became formalized to describe the entire surrounding region.
Today, locals alternate between the names Dantmara and Heyako, at times identifying the plantation as the Heyako Rubber Garden. The stretch of road leading to the garden is so beautiful that people call it "Selfie Road," and it draws many domestic tourists.
Fatikchhari is also home to three more rubber gardens, 18 tea estates (including the famed Halda Valley), and fertile farmlands growing an abundance of vegetables and fruits.
Across Bangladesh, there are 18 state-run rubber gardens encompassing a total land area of over 38,000 acres. Along with Dantmara, the largest of them all, the three other Fatikchhari gardens—Kanchannagar, Tarakho, and Rangamatia—cover over a fourth of Bangladesh’s total public-sector rubber plantations.
The Dantmara Rubber Garden predates Bangladesh itself; planting began during the late Pakistan era, though it did not come into commercial production until the late 1970s. Rubber trees cannot be harvested immediately. They must grow for five to seven years until they reach about six inches in diameter before their first tapping cycle can begin.
The process of actively extracting latex from rubber trees is called rubber tapping. It is a highly precise, delicate art requiring skilled laborers to slice into the bark without permanently damaging the tree. Tappers use a specialized, hooked tapping knife to shave a thin, downward diagonal groove along the bark at a 30- to 45-degree angle. This precise angle allows gravity to seamlessly channel the fluid. The cut is roughly a quarter of an inch deep—deep enough to open the latex-bearing vessels in the inner bark, but shallow enough to protect the delicate cambium layer, which is the tree’s internal growth zone. Cutting into the cambium can scar, stunt, or even kill the tree.
A small metal or ceramic spout is hammered into the bottom of the fresh incision. The milky-white, sticky liquid slowly oozes out, running down the spiral cut into the spout, which drips directly into a collection cup attached underneath. Tapping is almost exclusively done in the early morning hours, often before dawn. The cool morning temperatures maintain a higher internal fluid pressure inside the trunk, causing the latex to flow freely for up to five hours. As the sun rises and temperatures climb, the latex naturally thickens and coagulates, sealing the cut.
4 e The image shows a rubber tree plantation alongside the detailed process of rubber tapping. The left panel displays neatly arranged rows of rubber trees growing in a plantation setting while the focuses close up on a single trunk undergoing latex collection. A specialized diagonal incision is sliced into the bark, allowing the milky, white liquid sap (latex) to slowly drip down a metal spout into a small hanging cup. Photo: Dhaka Tribune/BFIDC
While surfing through the official website of the Bangladesh Forest Industries Development Corporation (BFIDC)—which operates the 18 state-run gardens—I found a fascinating history of rubber production. The natural forests of the Amazon Valley in South America are the original habitat of the rubber tree. Christopher Columbus is considered the first European to encounter rubber; after his second voyage in 1496, he brought back balls made from a type of tree gum, which the people of Haiti used for playing games.
Between 1873 and 1876, an enthusiastic group of British citizens gathered rubber seeds from Brazil and experimentally planted them in Kew Gardens, London. From there, about 2,000 seedlings were sent to present-day Sri Lanka, with subsequent seedlings distributed to Malaysia, the Java Islands, Singapore, and eventually India. Commercial rubber cultivation in the East began from these very seedlings. Singapore played a groundbreaking role by discovering a method of systematically extracting sap from the trees. Rubber is derived from latex, a substance in which rubber particles float in the form of colloidal oil. Roughly 25 to 30 percent of latex is rubber hydrocarbon, 60 percent is water, and the remainder consists of proteins, pigments, salts, and sugars.
According to the BFIDC, some seedlings were brought from the Calcutta Botanical Garden to Sylhet and Chittagong in 1910. Later, in 1952, the Forest Department planted experimental trees in Madhupur in Tangail, Hajerikhil in Chittagong, and Tetulia in Panchagarh. In 1959, Mr. Lloyd, an expert from the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), identified the climate and soil of the country as ideal for rubber cultivation. Following his recommendations, the Forest Department initiated a pilot project on 710 acres in 1960, establishing a 10-acre garden in Raozan, Chittagong, and a 30-acre garden in Ramu, Cox's Bazar, marking the official beginning of planned rubber cultivation in Bangladesh.
Returning from Chittagong to Dhaka after that 2022 visit, I found myself constantly thinking about how rewarding Fatikchhari had been, yet how much of it remained unexplored. Beyond the famous Dantmara garden, it boasts a diverse mix of lush tea estates, pristine wildlife sanctuaries, spiritual landmarks, and scenic modern hangouts. Fatikchhari is calling me back.

item.title: Radda clinic vandalized, looted in alleged takeover attempt
item.description:
The Radda MCH-FP Centre, which provides free and low-cost healthcare to disadvantaged and low-income people, was vandalized and looted by more than 200 people in Mirpur late Thursday night in what the institution described as an attempt to take over the facility.
The attackers allegedly held the centre’s security guards hostage, tied them up and then used hammers, an excavator, sticks and other equipment to demolish parts of the facility.
The centre authorities alleged that medicines, vaccines, government registers and documents, family planning supplies and other valuables were looted during the incident.
They said an ultrasound machine, generator, four air conditioners, four refrigerators and around Tk11.4 lakh in cash were among the items taken. The total damage was estimated at more than Tk1.5 crore, according to the institution.
Officials of the centre believe the incident was planned to take control of its 10-katha property.
Dr Nasrin Akhter, executive director of the Radda MCH-FP Centre, said more than 400 people receive healthcare services there on average every day, including disadvantaged mothers, children, adolescents and elderly people.
“They can no longer receive services from the centre following the vandalism,” she said.
Dr Nasrin alleged that an organization called "Somomona Samabaya Dokandar Samabay Samity" attempted to take over the centre.
“Our night guards were beaten and tied up. Their mobile phones and other belongings were taken. Later, the entire centre was vandalized using hammers, an excavator, sticks and other equipment,” she said.
She said the institution had obtained the right to provide healthcare services through an agreement with the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare in 1976 and had been providing free and low-cost services in partnership with the government for nearly 50 years.
“Our generator, four air conditioners, four refrigerators, an ultrasound machine, and various other equipment and instruments were there. The total damage will exceed Tk1.5 crore,” she said.
The centre authorities have filed a case with Shah Ali police station over the incident.
Officer-in-Charge Jahangir Alam said Hanif Mia was named in the case along with 200-250 unidentified people.
The accused have been charged with trespassing, theft, threats and causing damage worth more than Tk1.5 crore, he said.
Police are investigating the incident and attempting to identify and arrest those involved, the officer added.
A centre employee said several groups had previously claimed the property, but staff had received no prior warning that an attack was imminent.
The employee alleged that people associated with the "Somomona Samabaya Dokandar Samabay Samity" were involved but declined to name anyone.
Hanif Mia, a BNP leader from Mirpur, denied any involvement in the incident.
“I am not involved in this incident at all. I do not even know what happened there. Who put my name in the case? Please check with the police station about this,” he told reporters.

item.title: Investigating officer changed in Apratim murder case
item.description:
The investigating officer (IO) in the case filed over the murder of Ishayat Shahriar, alias Apratim, the only child of a Comilla University teacher, has been changed.
Inspector (Investigation) Rajib Ahmed of Sadar South Model Police Station will now investigate the case, replacing Sub-Inspector Saiful Islam.
Additional Superintendent of Police Md Lutfur Rahman confirmed the development on Friday night.
The case documents are expected to be handed over to Rajib within the next few days.
Rajib said the superintendent of police’s office had issued an order changing the investigating officer.
“Investigation will begin after we receive the case documents. We hope to complete the investigation soon and submit the charge sheet to the court at the earliest,” he said.
Apratim went missing from the Kotbari area of Comilla on the afternoon of September 18 after leaving home to take photos with his iPhone.
Police recovered his body the following day from a forested area in the Sananda area of Lalmai Hills.
Police said they have so far arrested Saiful Islam Tuhin, 19, Siam, 19, and two juveniles in connection with the murder, based on CCTV footage and information from Apratim’s mobile phone.
The two juveniles were sent to the Gazipur Child Development Centre by a court, while Tuhin and Siam are being held at Comilla Central Jail.

item.title: Fuel price hike pushes up transport fares in Chittagong
item.description:
Transport fares have gone up in Chittagong following the government’s latest fuel price hike, with commuters also facing a shortage of buses and human haulers on major city routes.
Minimum bus fares have increased by Tk3 to Tk10 and minibus fares by Tk3 to Tk8. On the Dhaka-Chittagong route, fares have risen by up to Tk100.
The fare hike officially applies to diesel-run public transport. However, passengers said fares for CNG-run minibuses and tempos on city Route 3 had also increased by Tk2, from Tk5 to Tk7.
The higher fares came as commuters struggled to find public transport. Large crowds were seen waiting at Muradpur, Bahaddarhat, Sholoshahar, Gate No 2, GEC and Agrabad on Thursday.
At around 9am in Muradpur, scores of passengers waited along the roadside. Whenever a bus or human hauler arrived, passengers rushed to board. Many could not get on as the vehicles were already packed.
Nurul Islam, who was waiting to travel to Agrabad, said he had already spent around 30 minutes waiting. “There are not enough public transport vehicles. The ones that are coming are overcrowded, so I cannot get on,” he said.
Mohammad Musa, another passenger, said the transport shortage had persisted since morning, while operators were charging higher fares, citing increased fuel prices.
Passengers travelling from Muradpur to the Kotwali intersection have been particularly affected. Apart from maxi services, few public transport vehicles operate on the route.
Belayet Hossain Belal, president of the Chittagong Metropolitan Transport Owners’ Group, said around 70% of public transport vehicles operating in the city were used to carry workers to industrial establishments.
“As a result, commuters face a shortage of public transport during office hours in the morning and afternoon,” he said. The issue had been raised several times with the authorities, but no solution had been found, he added.
Shahidul Islam, vice-president of the group, said no fare increase had been made for CNG-run public transport. The city has around 1,300 buses on 18 routes and 1,800-1,900 human haulers on 22 routes, according to him.
Meanwhile, fares on the Dhaka-Chittagong route have also increased. A bus fare that was previously Tk700 is now Tk800 on some services.
Kafil Uddin, general secretary of the Inter-District Bus Owners’ Association, said fares had been increased because of higher fuel costs. Some services were charging Tk758, compared with Tk700 previously, he added.
The government recently announced a Tk20-per-litre increase in the prices of diesel, kerosene, octane and petrol.

item.title: Police: Nasiruddin Patwary should be questioned over crude bomb remarks
item.description:
Police believe National Citizen Party (NCP) Chief Coordinator Nasiruddin Patwary should be questioned over his recent remarks concerning a series of crude bomb explosions in different parts of the capital.
Mohammad Tofail Ahmed Mia, joint commissioner (Crime Prevention-South) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP), made the comment at a press conference on the recovery of explosives and masks at the DMP Media Centre on Minto Road on Friday afternoon.
Asked about Patwary’s comments, the police official said: “I think he should be questioned.”
Following a recent protest procession in the capital, Patwary said that there would be no more explosions in Dhaka if the government accepted the party’s three main demands.
Referring to the statement, journalists asked whether the recent crude bomb explosions were being carried out only by leaders and activists of banned organisations or whether others were also involved.
Tofail Ahmed said Patwary should be questioned about why he made such a statement.
“I think he should definitely be questioned,” he said.
Asked whether police could question Patwary, the joint commissioner said the matter would have to be decided by senior officials.
Earlier, police arrested a man and recovered explosives, materials used to make cocktails and 9,000 paper masks allegedly prepared for criminal purposes during a raid in South Keraniganj.
The arrested man was identified as Jahid Hasan Emon. The operation was conducted by police from Shyampur Model Police Station.

Six-year-old girl raped, killed in Brahmanbaria
item.description:
A six-year-old girl was raped and killed in Ashuganj upazila of Brahmanbaria on Friday afternoon, with locals later detaining and beating the suspected perpetrator before handing him over to police.
The incident took place in Andidil village, Paschim Talsahar Union around noon.
The deceased was the daughter of expatriate Mozammel Haque, a resident of the village. The incident has triggered tension in the area.
According to the girl’s relatives, the child was called away by Jahidul, a teenager from a neighbouring house, while prayers were underway around noon.
When the girl did not return home, her mother began searching for her. She reportedly became suspicious after finding her daughter’s shoes in front of Jahidul’s uncle’s house.
Jahidul allegedly told the mother that he had given the girl water before she went elsewhere.
Suspecting that her daughter might be inside the house, the mother reportedly forced her way in and found the child lying motionless. She raised an alarm, prompting neighbours to rush to the scene, while Jahidul fled.
Locals later caught him and detained him at his uncle’s house. When an angry crowd attempted to attack him, additional police from Ashuganj arrived and took him to the police station.
Dr Monir Hossain, a physician at the 250-bed Brahmanbaria General Hospital, said the girl was brought to the hospital dead.
He said there were marks of injuries on different parts of her body and that a history of rape was suspected. Doctors subsequently recommended a post-mortem examination.
Jahangir Alam, assistant superintendent of police of Sarail Circle, said Jahidul confessed to the incident after being detained by police.
The body has been kept at the district headquarters hospital morgue for autopsy.

Three held with 960 sacks of urea fertilizer bound for Myanmar
item.description:
The Coast Guard has detained three alleged smugglers and seized 960 sacks of urea fertilizer while they were being smuggled to Myanmar from Mirsarai in Chittagong.
Coast Guard media officer Lt Commander Sabbir Alam Sujon disclosed the information in a press release on Friday afternoon. He said a special operation was conducted around 1am on Thursday near Ichakhali Ghat in Mirsarai by the Coast Guard Station.
During the operation, Coast Guard personnel seized 960 sacks, or 48,000kg, of urea fertilizer worth around Tk3.36 million. The fertilizer was being transferred from trucks to a fishing boat for illegal shipment to Myanmar.
The operation also led to the detention of three alleged smugglers and the seizure of four trucks and a fishing boat used in the smuggling operation.
Legal action has been taken against the seized fertilizer, vehicles, boat and detainees in the presence of an executive magistrate, the Coast Guard said.

item.title: CHT minister: Concerted efforts needed to curb drugs, border crimes
item.description:
Chittagong Hill Tracts Affairs Minister Sa Ching Prue has stressed coordinated efforts by the media and law enforcement agencies to address drug trafficking, border crimes and challenges related to refugees.
“Cox’s Bazar and the Chittagong Hill Tracts share close geographical and social ties. We are committed to developing Cox’s Bazar into a modern tourism city through a well-planned master plan,” the minister said.
He made the remarks while speaking at a view-exchange meeting with journalists at the Cox’s Bazar Press Club on Friday.
He said the government would work to expand tourism in Cox’s Bazar, Bandarban and other parts of the country and promote the sector at home and abroad. Expressing concern over drug trafficking, Sa Ching Prue said drugs entering the country through roads and waterways were spreading across society.
He called for drug-prevention committees in every neighbourhood in line with the Home Minister’s call. Regarding the Rohingya crisis and border crimes, he said some Rohingyas were becoming involved in drug trafficking, smuggling, human trafficking and illegal arms trading.
He proposed jointly formulating specific recommendations with the Home Ministry, law enforcement agencies and journalists and presenting them to the prime minister to address the crisis. The minister said Cox’s Bazar could be transformed into a world-class tourism city by utilizing its sea beach and the natural diversity of the hill region.
Praising journalists as the “conscience of society,” he urged them to present objective news and pledged to work for socioeconomic development.
Cox’s Bazar Press Club President Mahbubur Rahman chaired the meeting. Senior local journalists also attended.

item.title: Rayan header salvages 1-1 draw between Brazil and Australia
item.description:
A last minute header from Brazilian substitute Rayan salvaged a 1-1 draw with Australia in a thrilling international friendly in Townsville on Friday.
Rayan headed the ball home in the 95th minute to deny the hosts what would have been only their second win over the South American giants.
It was a fitting result from two evenly-matched teams who gave everything in front of a sell-out crowd in the North Queensland city.
"It was a difficult game," Brazil manager Carlo Ancelotti conceded.
"The pitch was not so good to play good football on, but we showed fight until the end.
"I think it was a good test for us."
A superb free kick from Australian youngster Nestory Irankunda had looked enough to give the Socceroos an upset win.
With the two sides locked at 0-0 midway through the second half, Irankunda stepped up and drilled his free kick over the defensive wall into the net, leaving Brazil keeper Hugo Souza rooted to the spot.
But Brazil came out and dominated against an increasingly defensive Australian outfit and were rewarded seconds before full-time.
With both teams looking to rebuild after early exits from this year's World Cup, it was the Socceroos who seized the early advantage.
They dominated possession and territory, attacking with width and finding plenty of space on both sides.
Midfielder Connor Metcalfe went close in just the third minute before an Irankunda bullet forced a good save from Souza.
Brazil weathered the storm and began to get into the game, looking increasingly dangerous through in-form Barcelona striker Raphinha and Chelsea forward Estevao.
Raphinha had a good chance with a header straight to Australian keeper Patrick Beach after 20 minutes before Estevao forced a great save from Beach five minutes later.
The Brazil dominance appeared to have paid off in the 46th minute when Estevao scored, but a VAR review saw the goal ruled out due to an earlier foul on Australian captain Harry Soutar.
The second half saw much of the same, with Brazil controlling the centre and the Socceroos finding space out wide.
The visitors were just edging the match and it seemed only a matter of time before they scored, but they were shocked by Irankunda's superb free kick.
The Socceroos defended furiously and looked to have held out for the win, but a last minute corner saw Rayan's header just too powerful for Beach to hold out.

item.title: Bashundhara SuperGolf opens in Dhaka
item.description:
Bashundhara SuperGolf, a new sports and entertainment facility, was officially inaugurated in Dhaka on Thursday, with the venue aiming to make golf more accessible while offering a wider range of recreational and social activities.
Located near Madani Avenue, the facility was inaugurated at a ceremony attended by Bashundhara Group Chairman Ahmed Akbar Sobhan, Sanvir Bashundhara Group Chairman Shafiat Sobhan Sanvir, Tanvir Bashundhara Group Managing Director Ahmed Ibrahim Sobhan and Sanvir Bashundhara Group and Bashundhara SuperGolf Managing Director Aemil Ahmed Sobhan.
Business leaders, corporate representatives, sports and cultural personalities and members of the media were also present at the event.
Built around the concept of “More than just golf,” Bashundhara SuperGolf features 107 golf bays equipped with digital tracking technology.
The three-level facility also includes restaurants, a café, pro shop, golf simulator, training rooms, billiards facilities, VIP suites, meeting rooms, an event hall, a kids’ zone and a sports lounge.
Speaking at the inauguration, Aemil Ahmed Sobhan said the project was designed to offer visitors an experience beyond conventional golf facilities.
“Our main objective was to create a modern space where people can enjoy not only professional golf practice but also food, entertainment and social activities with their families, friends and corporate teams,” he said.
He said the facility had been planned and developed over more than a year, with an emphasis on providing international-standard services.
Rezaur Rahman, head of operations at Bashundhara SuperGolf, and Ahmed Ibrahim Sobhan also spoke at the event, highlighting the facility's range of services and its potential contribution to sports, recreation and the broader economy.
Following the inauguration, guests toured the different floors and facilities of the venue.
According to the management, Bashundhara SuperGolf will offer both annual membership and pay-and-play options, allowing visitors to use the golf facilities without taking an annual membership.
The facility is expected to cater to golf enthusiasts as well as families, young people and corporate groups, combining golf, dining, entertainment and social events at a single venue.
The management said the facility aims to contribute to the wider development and accessibility of golf in Bangladesh while establishing a new destination for sports and recreation in Dhaka.

item.title: Asian Games 2026: Imranur bows out in 100m semifinal
item.description:
Bangladesh's fastest sprinter Imranur Rahman bowed out of the men's 100m at the Asian Games 2026 after finishing seventh in the first semifinal heat in Japan on Friday.
Imranur clocked 10.44 seconds, improving slightly on his 10.49 second effort in Thursday's first round, where he finished 22nd among the 24 athletes who advanced to the semifinals.
Despite the improvement, Imranur described the race as one of his worst of the year, saying his performance should be viewed in the context of his return from a two-year injury layoff.
He said athletes cannot produce their best time in every race but was relieved that the injury had not worsened.
Imranur said he would review the race, identify his mistakes and work to return stronger.
His semifinal appearance marked another step in his comeback, although he could not advance to the final.

item.title: State minister: Gas supply disrupted due to delayed LNG unloading
item.description:
Gas pressure had temporarily dropped due to a delay in unloading gas from an LNG carrier amid rough weather in the Bay of Bengal, State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Aninda Islam Amit said on Friday.
However, the unloading process resumed at 7:18am and gas supply would return to normal by noon, he said.
The state minister made the remarks in response to questions from journalists after a district hospital health management meeting at the Jessore Circuit House on Friday afternoon.
He also said Bangladesh would benefit if fuel prices in the international market stabilise.
Speaking about ongoing health sector initiatives in Jessore, Amit said residents would receive services from a full-fledged coronary care unit (CCU) within the stipulated timeframe.
“The government is working to ensure that critically ill heart patients no longer have to travel to other districts for treatment,” he said.
He said the meeting reviewed progress in implementing decisions taken at an earlier meeting to improve healthcare services at the 250-bed Jessore General Hospital.
“Most of the decisions have made good progress, while deadlines have been set for the remaining work. Within the next few months, we will ensure that people in remote areas have access to improved healthcare services,” he said.

item.title: Ahmed Azam: Govt cannot be toppled through threats
item.description:
Liberation War Affairs Minister Ahmed Azam Khan on Friday said the government cannot be toppled by issuing threats and warnings, as it is a government elected by the people.
“This government is the government of the people. This government is a democratic government. This government is a government elected by the people. It cannot be toppled through threats and intimidation,” he said.
The minister was speaking at a rally organized by the Jatiyatabadi Tati Dal in front of the Jatiya Press Club before a procession.
He said Prime Minister Tarique Rahman always seeks cooperation from the opposition over the issues they raise in parliament.
“Come, let us turn parliament into the center of all politics, all development and all prosperity. Criticize us if we make mistakes; we will correct ourselves. We will build this country with you,” Ahmed Azam quoted the prime minister as saying.
“But we are noticing that whatever the opposition says in parliament, outside parliament, they are trying hard to destabilize the government and the country. This reminds us of what Sheikh Hasina said in 1991. Sheikh Hasina said, I will not allow an elected government to remain in peace even for a minute,” he said.
The minister said the current opposition might not be using those exact words, but its activities seven months into the government’s tenure, including long marches and threats to topple and remove the government and not to leave the streets, indicate that it is following Sheikh Hasina’s approach step by step.
He, however, said the people do not like it.
Ahmed Azam said people want free and fair elections every five years under a caretaker government.
“They want elections where there will be no ballot stuffing, no coercion, no threats or intimidation. People will cast their votes; there will be no voting at night. Those who are elected by the people’s votes will serve the country for the next five years,” he said.
“We did not take responsibility to rule the country. We have taken responsibility in government to serve the country,” the minister said.
He said the opposition appears to believe that the government will fall simply by issuing threats.
The minister urged the opposition to refrain from what he described as the politics of sabotage, arson and threats.
“So, I will tell you clearly, refrain from the politics of sabotage, arson and threats like before. Speak in parliament. If we make mistakes, point them out in parliament,” he said.

item.title: Farhaan to make debut as Bangladesh make six changes against Malaysia
item.description:
Thomas Dooley made six changes to his second starting XI in charge of Bangladesh for their FIFA ASEAN Cup opener against Malaysia on Friday, handing Farhaan Ali Wahid his international debut.
Bangladesh’s last match was against hosts San Marino on June 5, when they secured a 2-1 victory.
Goalkeeper Mehedi Hasan Srabon, defenders Shakil Ahad Topu and Zayyan Ahmed, and midfielders Shamit Shome, Fahamedul Islam and Farhaan Ali Wahid came into the starting XI.
They replaced Mitul Marma, Topu Barman, Isa Faysal, Jamal Bhuiyan, Sheikh Morsalin and Rafiqul Islam, while Faysal Ahmed Fahim also came into the side, making it six changes in total, with Bangladesh lining up in a 4-2-3-1 formation.
The match kicks off at the Gelora Bung Karno Stadium in Jakarta at 3pm Bangladesh time.
The men in red and green will face Singapore on September 28 at the same venue before taking on hosts Indonesia in their final group-stage match on October 1.

item.title: Harimoto hails new era as Japan dethrone China's table tennis kings
item.description:
Tomokazu Harimoto said Japan had overcome their inferiority complex after ending table tennis powerhouse China's 32-year run as Asian Games men's team champions in a nail-biting final.
China had won gold in the event at every Games since 1994 but they were dethroned by Japan after Sora Matsushima beat Wen Ruibo in the decisive match to win 3-2.
The Japan team also featured Harimoto, whose parents were both born in China and whose mother once represented the country at the world championships.
"That we beat them was proof that we had lacked confidence before," said Harimoto, whose sister Miwa plays for Japan's women's team.
"I'm happy, but looking at the actual contest, there was nothing unusual about the way we played or the outcome.
"We just managed to attain the one thing we'd been missing -- confidence."
China's team featured world number one Wang Chuqin but his team-mates Lin Shidong and Wen are respectively ranked eighth and 15th in the world.
Japan had two top-five players in number three Matsushima and number four Harimoto.
"China used to have six or seven strong players, that's why their era lasted 10 or 20 years," said Harimoto.
"Now with two of us in the world top five, Matsushima and I can win like this."
Harimoto could not bring himself to watch the final match from the team bench after beating Wang to level it at 2-2.
"I thought it was better not to go back, a bit like a superstition," said Harimoto.
"If I was on the bench, Matsushima would see me. He probably wouldn't mind, but I minded."
Wang won the opening match against Matsushima but lost 3-0 against Harimoto.
The Chinese player said: "Psychologically, I ran into problems".
"Perhaps we panicked a little in trying to be better, and rushed some shots," he said.
China got their own back in the women's team final, beating Japan 3-0.
But the men's defeat left a bitter taste in the mouths of Chinese fans, who vented their anger on social media.
"The men's team, despite enjoying the best resources and treatment, suffers from lack of continuity and a talent gap," one user wrote on Weibo.
"There is no one coming through," wrote another.

item.title: Women’s hockey team secure historic Asian Games point after thrilling draw
item.description:
Bangladesh national women’s hockey team earned their first-ever point in their Asian Games debut after holding Kazakhstan to a thrilling 3-3 draw in Gifu, Japan on Friday.
Airin Riya, Kona Akter and Orpita Pal scored one goal each for Bangladesh, while Viktoriya Lobanova completed a hat-trick for Kazakhstan in an entertaining Pool A encounter.
Riya gave Bangladesh an early lead, converting from a penalty corner in the second minute. The lead lasted until the 21st minute, when Viktoriya levelled the score.
Viktoriya struck again in the 32nd minute to put Kazakhstan ahead, but Kona restored parity in the 40th minute.
Viktoriya completed her hat-trick in the 37th minute before Orpita brought Bangladesh level again with a penalty-corner goal in the 47th minute.
Bangladesh earned 10 penalty corners during the match, compared with Kazakhstan’s three.
The draw ended a difficult start to the campaign for the women in red and green, who had suffered heavy defeats against China (13-0), Malaysia (3-1) and South Korea (8-0) in their first three Pool A matches.
Bangladesh will face Chinese Taipei in their final group fixture on Sunday.

item.title: Mahdi: PM’s UNGA engagements focus on Bangladesh’s interests, global cooperation
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s engagements during his visit to New York have focused on advancing Bangladesh’s interests, strengthening regional and global cooperation, and presenting the country’s priorities on the world stage, PM’s Adviser Mahdi Amin said on Thursday.
He made the remarks at a press briefing at the United Nations headquarters in New York after the Prime Minister’s engagements on the third day of his visit to attend the 81st session of the UN General Assembly.
Mahdi said the Prime Minister’s programmes on the day covered multilateral engagements, high-level bilateral meetings and two thematic events on climate change and health.
He said Tarique held meetings with the prime ministers of Pakistan and Thailand, where they discussed ways to strengthen regional cooperation and people-to-people ties based on equality, fairness and mutual respect.
At a high-level meeting on the threats posed by sea-level rise, the spokesperson said the Prime Minister highlighted Bangladesh’s environmental priorities, including a plan to plant 250 million trees over five years and dredge more than 20,000 kilometres of canals.
He also presented plans concerning the proposed Padma Barrage and Teesta mega plan and put forward four proposals aimed at addressing climate-related challenges.
At another high-level event on integrating midwifery into primary healthcare, Mahdi said the Prime Minister outlined Bangladesh’s plans to reduce maternal and child mortality and expand healthcare services at the grassroots level.
He said the Prime Minister wants to ensure healthcare reaches every family, particularly in rural and marginalised communities.
Mahdi also highlighted Tarique’s meeting with UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, describing it as a “very fruitful” meeting.
He said the UN chief congratulated the Prime Minister on his electoral victory and the return of Bangladesh to a democratic system through what he described as a peaceful and acceptable election.
According to Mahdi, Guterres thanked Bangladesh for hosting Rohingyas and for the contribution of its military personnel to UN peacekeeping operations.
He also appreciated Bangladesh’s role in climate resilience and its contribution to multilateralism, he said.
During the meeting, Tarique discussed Bangladesh’s role in global peacekeeping and multilateral cooperation and expressed his interest in strengthening the country’s engagement with the United Nations, Mahdi said.
He said the Prime Minister’s address to the General Assembly reflected Bangladesh’s priorities on global peace, Palestine, democracy, human rights and the rule of law, as well as inclusive development.
Tarique also outlined his government’s policy priorities on health, education, agriculture, employment, technology and the environment, including the Family Card, Farmer Card, e-Health Card and a proposed universal card, Mahdi said.
“The Prime Minister presented a roadmap for building a prosperous, self-reliant and welfare-oriented Bangladesh,” he said.
Mahdi said the Prime Minister also spoke about strengthening democracy and the rule of law and ensuring human rights.
He said the Prime Minister’s UNGA address went beyond Bangladesh’s national interests and highlighted issues of global peace and cooperation.
Referring to the Prime Minister’s participation in the UN General Assembly, Mahdi said it was also significant that Tarique was the third member of his family to represent Bangladesh at the world body, following his father Ziaur Rahman and mother Khaleda Zia.
He also noted that Bangladesh’s Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman is presiding over the 81st UN General Assembly.
Mahdi said the Prime Minister has been maintaining a busy schedule throughout his four-day New York visit, attending programmes from morning until late in the day.
The Prime Minister arrived in New York on Monday to attend the 81st session of the UN General Assembly. He is scheduled to return to Dhaka on Sunday.
